subject: What after a Pearson's r linear regression?

messages.author: 45e4d261cc3d645c
messages.subject: What after a Pearson's r linear regression?
parts:
Hi!

While reading the book and trying things out with my own data, I happened to come up with a big question that is related to methodological correctness.

First of all, I wanted to test the correlation between two ratio variables, nl. the frequency of one construction and the frequency of its nominal element in a corpus. After computing the correlation coefficient, I arrived at the following results:

- r: 0.95 (very high correlation);
- r squared: 91.31;
- Kendall's tau (less sensitive to outliers): 0.64 (high correlation).

1) Should I test whether this correlation is statistically significant? e.g. cor.test (SFLWR, p. 241). Following the graph that visualizes the search process, there seems to be no further step. 

However, when applying the Shapiro test to see whether both vectors are normally distributed, the p-value of the respective vectors differ significantly from a normality. In this case, a non-parametric test should be applied, e.g. Fligner-Killeen. When I try this, I obtain NAs:

> fligner.test(IPV~PLAATS)

Fligner-Killeen test of homogeneity of variances

data:  IPV by PLAATS
Fligner-Killeen:med chi-squared = NaN, df = 9, p-value = NA

I thank the kind soul(s) in advance.

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] What after a Pearson's r linear regression?
parts: > First of all, I wanted to test the correlation between two ratio variables
> 1) Should I test whether this correlation is statistically significant?

Well, do you want to know whether it is statistically significantly
different from 0?

> However, when applying the Shapiro test to see whether both vectors are normally distributed, the p-value of the respective vectors differ significantly from a normality. In this case, a non-parametric test should be applied, e.g. Fligner-Killeen.

Fligner-Killeen is not a non-parametric alternative to a correlation
test but to an F-test - Kendall's tau would be more appropriate.

STG

Ok for kendall's tau.
